# Integration Test Suite for Order Fulfillment System

```python
import pytest
from testcontainers.compose import DockerCompose
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch
import asyncio

# ============================================
# FIXTURES
# ============================================

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def services():
    """Spin up all services via docker-compose."""
    with DockerCompose(".", compose_file_name="docker-compose.test.yml") as compose:
        compose.wait_for("http://localhost:8080/health")
        yield compose

@pytest.fixture
def order_client(services):
    """HTTP client for Order Service."""
    return OrderServiceClient("http://localhost:8080")

@pytest.fixture
def test_order():
    """Isolated test data with unique ID."""
    return {
        "order_id": f"test-{uuid.uuid4()}",
        "items": [{"sku": "WIDGET-001", "qty": 2}],
        "payment": {"method": "card", "token": "tok_test"}
    }

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
async def cleanup(order_client, test_order):
    """Cleanup after each test."""
    yield
    await order_client.force_cancel(test_order["order_id"])

# ============================================
# HAPPY PATH
# ============================================

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_complete_order_flow(order_client, test_order):
    """Full order succeeds: inventory reserved, payment charged, notification sent."""
    result = await order_client.place_order(test_order)
    
    assert result.status == "CONFIRMED"
    assert result.inventory_reserved == True
    assert result.payment_charged == True
    assert result.notification_sent == True

# ============================================
# SERVICE FAILURE SCENARIOS
# ============================================

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_inventory_unavailable_triggers_rejection(order_client, test_order):
    """Order rejected when inventory insufficient - no payment attempted."""
    test_order["items"][0]["qty"] = 99999
    
    result = await order_client.place_order(test_order)
    
    assert result.status == "REJECTED"
    assert result.reason == "INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY"
    assert result.payment_charged == False

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_payment_failure_unreserves_inventory(order_client, test_order):
    """Payment failure triggers inventory compensation."""
    test_order["payment"]["token"] = "tok_decline"
    
    result = await order_client.place_order(test_order)
    
    assert result.status == "FAILED"
    assert result.inventory_released == True  # Compensating txn

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_notification_failure_does_not_rollback(order_client, test_order):
    """Notification is non-critical; order stays confirmed."""
    with patch_notification_service(raise_error=True):
        result = await order_client.place_order(test_order)
    
    assert result.status == "CONFIRMED"
    assert result.notification_sent == False

# ============================================
# TIMEOUT & RETRY
# ============================================

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_inventory_timeout_retries_then_fails(order_client, test_order):
    """Retries 3x on timeout, then fails gracefully."""
    with patch_inventory_service(delay_ms=5000):
        result = await order_client.place_order(test_order, timeout=1)
    
    assert result.status == "FAILED"
    assert result.retry_count == 3

# ============================================
# ASYNC MESSAGE HANDLING
# ============================================

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_out_of_order_messages_handled(order_client, message_queue):
    """System handles payment confirmation arriving before inventory ack."""
    await message_queue.publish("payment.success", order_id="123")
    await message_queue.publish("inventory.reserved", order_id="123")
    
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    order = await order_client.get_order("123")
    
    assert order.status == "CONFIRMED"

# ============================================
# DATA ISOLATION
# ============================================

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_concurrent_orders_isolated(order_client):
    """Parallel orders don't interfere with each other."""
    orders = [{"order_id": f"concurrent-{i}", ...} for i in range(10)]
    
    results = await asyncio.gather(*[
        order_client.place_order(o) for o in orders
    ])
    
    assert all(r.status == "CONFIRMED" for r in results)
```

**Key patterns:** Testcontainers for real services, unique IDs for isolation, autouse cleanup, async-first design, explicit compensation verification.
